obligations.text: Before an overdraft fee is charged on a card or app transaction, a firm must show the consumer the fee amount and give a choice to cancel the transaction.
A firm must send each consumer a monthly summary of all overdraft and returned-item fees charged in the previous month, with a year-to-date total.

RCN-2026-002.title: Responding to customer data access requests

obligations.text: A firm must respond to a customer data access request within 30 calendar days of receiving it, providing a copy of the personal data held.
A firm must keep a log of every data access request, including the date received, the date answered and the outcome.

RCN-2026-003.title: Operational resilience of important business services

obligations.text: A firm must identify its important business services and set an impact tolerance for the maximum tolerable disruption of each.
A firm must test its ability to remain within impact tolerance through severe but plausible scenario exercises at least once a year.
The board must approve the list of important business services and impact tolerances each year.
A firm must acknowledge a complaint in writing within 2 business days of receiving it.
A firm must send the customer a final response within 15 business days of receiving a complaint.
A firm must analyze the root causes of complaints at least quarterly and report the findings to senior management.
A firm must identify and verify every individual who owns 25 percent or more of a business customer before opening the account.
A firm must refresh beneficial ownership information for high-risk business customers at least once a year.

RCN-2026-006.title: Reimbursement for authorized push payment scams

obligations.text: A firm must reimburse an eligible scam victim within 5 business days of the claim, unless it has evidence of gross negligence or first-party fraud.
A firm must check the payee name against the account and show the customer a warning when the name does not match before a first payment to a new payee.
A firm must retain records of each complaint, including all correspondence with the customer, for at least 7 years from the final response.
A firm must provide complaint records to the Authority within 10 business days of a request.
A firm must notify the Financial Data Protection Office of a personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
A firm must notify affected customers without undue delay when a breach is likely to put them at high risk.
A firm must keep a register of third parties that support important business services.
A firm must maintain a tested exit plan for each critical third-party arrangement.
A firm must review the performance and risk of each critical third party at least once a year.
A firm must record, with the customer's consent, any vulnerability a customer discloses, so that staff can adapt how they serve that customer.
A firm must train customer-facing staff to recognize and respond to signs of vulnerability at least once a year.

RCN-2026-011.title: Third-party AI models in credit decisions

obligations.text: A firm must maintain an inventory of third-party AI models used in consumer credit decisions, recording the supplier, purpose and the products affected.
The model risk committee must review each third-party AI model in the inventory at least once a year, including its performance and fairness results.
A firm must file a suspicious activity report within 30 calendar days of first detecting the suspicious activity.
A firm must report suspicious activity reporting volumes and timeliness to the board at least quarterly.
A card issuer must show on each monthly statement how long it would take to repay the balance by paying only the minimum, and the total interest that would be paid.
A firm must screen outgoing instant payments for fraud in real time, before the payment is released.
A firm must give customers a way to report fraud that is available 24 hours a day, every day.
A firm must run liquidity stress tests at least monthly, including a scenario with rapid outflows of digital deposits.
A firm must hold enough liquid assets to cover the net outflows of its most severe stress scenario for at least 30 days.
An insurer or insurance intermediary must complete a written suitability assessment before recommending an annuity to a consumer.
An insurer must disclose surrender charges and the surrender period before the consumer signs an annuity contract.

RCN-2026-017.title: Best execution reporting for equity orders

obligations.text: A broker-dealer must publish a quarterly report on the venues to which it routed customer equity orders and the execution quality obtained.
A firm must offer statements and important notices in large print, braille or a screen-reader friendly format on request, at no extra cost.
A firm must keep a record of when and how each customer gave consent to electronic marketing.
A firm must stop sending electronic marketing within 10 days after a customer withdraws consent.
A firm must contact a mortgage borrower within 15 calendar days after a payment is missed.
A firm must offer a borrower in financial difficulty forbearance options, such as a temporary payment reduction, before starting repossession proceedings.
A firm must screen its customer base against each update to the sanctions list within 24 hours of the update being published.
A firm must report a significant cyber incident to the Prudential Banking Board within 24 hours of determining that the incident is significant.
A firm must send the Prudential Banking Board a final incident report with root cause and remediation within 30 days after the incident is resolved.
A firm must not call a consumer about a particular debt more than 7 times within 7 days.
A firm must honor a consumer's request to be contacted only in writing.
A firm must post a notice in its app and on its website within 1 hour of an outage that prevents customers from making payments.
A firm must give consumers at least 60 days' written notice before increasing a fee on a deposit account.
